title: CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
chineseTitle: 第 23 章：荣誉之战中的挫折

paragraphs.en: Anne faced more than two weeks of trouble. A month after the liniment cake incident, she made a mistake by accidentally pouring milk into yarn balls instead of pig feed. She also fell into a brook while daydreaming on a log bridge.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮为此事烦恼了两周多。一个月后，她在处理猪饲料时不小心将牛奶倒在了纱球上，而不是猪食里。此外，她还在桥墩上的木板上发呆时失足掉进了小溪中。

paragraphs.en: A week after the manse tea party, Diana Barry hosted another gathering for their class. They enjoyed themselves but grew restless as the evening wore on. The girls were eager for some mischief, and "daring" soon became their game of choice.
paragraphs.zh: 在牧师住宅茶会之后的一个星期，戴安娜·巴瑞又为她们的班级举办了一场聚会。大家玩得很开心，但随着夜晚的推移，渐渐感到有些无聊。女孩子们渴望搞点恶作剧，于是“大胆尝试”成了她们的游戏首选。

paragraphs.en: Daring was popular among Avonlea's young people that summer. Carrie Sloane dared Ruby Gillis to climb a large willow tree near the front door. Despite her fear of caterpillars and her mother’s disapproval, Ruby managed to reach the top, much to Carrie's embarrassment.
paragraphs.zh: 那个夏天，在埃文利的年轻人中，大胆的行为颇受欢迎。卡莉·斯洛恩敢让鲁比·吉尔思爬上靠近前门的一棵大柳树。尽管她害怕毛虫，而且母亲也不赞成，鲁比还是成功地爬到了树顶，这让卡莉感到十分尴尬。

paragraphs.en: Josie Pye then dared Jane Andrews to hop on one leg around the garden without stopping or touching the ground with her right foot. Jane tried but gave up after three corners, admitting defeat.
paragraphs.zh: 乔西·派伊竟敢向简·安德鲁斯下战书，让她单脚跳绕花园一圈，中途不能停下也不能用右脚触地。简试了三次，只绕了三个角落便放弃了，承认自己输了。

paragraphs.en: Anne challenged Josie Pye to walk along the top of the board fence in their garden. Josie, despite her lack of popularity, had a natural talent for this skill. She walked the Barry fence with ease and confidence, earning reluctant admiration from the other girls.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮向乔西·派耶发起挑战，让她在花园里的木板围栏顶上行走。尽管乔西不怎么受欢迎，但她天生就有这项技能。她轻松自信地走过了巴里家的围栏，赢得了其他女孩们勉强给予的钦佩。

paragraphs.en: Josie descended, flushed with victory, and looked at Anne defiantly. Anne dismissed the challenge, saying it was not particularly impressive to walk a low board fence. She recalled a girl in Marysville who could even walk a roof ridgepole.
paragraphs.zh: 乔西满面通红，得意洋洋地走了下来，挑衅地看着安妮。安妮轻描淡写地回应说，这不过是走一道低矮的围栏，并不算什么了不起的事。她还想起玛丽维尔的一个女孩，竟然能走在屋顶的椽子上。

paragraphs.en: Josie flatly disagreed, challenging Anne to climb up and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof. Anne turned pale but knew she had no choice. Diana pleaded with her not to do it, warning that she might fall and be killed.
paragraphs.zh: 乔西断然不同意，主动向安妮挑战，让她上去走一走巴里先生厨房屋顶上的那根椽子。安妮的脸色顿时变得苍白，但她知道自己别无选择。戴安娜央求她不要这么做，并警告说她可能会摔下来，性命不保。

paragraphs.en: However, Anne insisted on doing it for her honor.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，安妮坚持要为自己的荣誉去做这件事。

paragraphs.en: Anne climbed the ladder silently, reached the ridgepole, and began walking along it, feeling dizzy and high up. Despite the danger, she managed a few steps before losing balance and falling off the roof, sliding down through the Virginia creeper below.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮悄无声息地爬上了梯子，来到房梁上，开始沿着它行走，感到头晕目眩，高高在上。尽管危险重重，她还是走了几步，最终失去平衡，从屋顶摔了下去，顺着下面的紫藤滑了下来。

paragraphs.en: Anne narrowly escaped a serious injury when she fell from the roof. Fortunately, she landed on the side where the roof extended close to the ground, making her fall less dangerous. Upon discovering Anne lying unconscious among the debris of Virginia creeper vines, Diana and the other girls rushed around the house in panic—except Ruby Gillis, who stood rooted to the spot and broke down into hysterics.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮差一点受了重伤，她在屋顶上失足跌落。幸运的是，她落在了屋顶接近地面的一侧，使得坠落的风险大大降低。当戴安娜和其他女孩在一片狼藉的紫藤残枝败叶中发现安妮昏迷不醒时，她们慌忙跑向房子周围——只有鲁比·吉尔思像根木桩一样站在原地，顿时歇斯底里地哭了起来。

paragraphs.en: Diana knelt beside Anne, crying out anxiously, "Anne, are you killed?" Anne managed to sit up dizzily and replied uncertainly, "No, Diana, I am not killed, but I think I'm unconscious."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜焦急地跪在安妮身旁，喊道：“安妮，你被杀了没？”安妮头晕目眩地勉强坐了起来，不确定地说：“不，戴安娜，我没死，但我感觉自己昏过去了。”

paragraphs.en: Carrie Sloane sobbed, "Where? Oh, where, Anne?" Before Anne could answer, Mrs. Barry arrived.
paragraphs.zh: 卡莉·斯洛恩抽泣着问道：“在哪里？哦，安妮，你在哪儿？”还没等安妮回答，巴里太太已经到了。

paragraphs.en: Anne tried to stand but cried out in pain when she failed.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮试图站起来，但一失败便痛呼出声。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Barry asked urgently, "What's the matter? Where have you hurt yourself?" Anne gasped, "My ankle."
paragraphs.zh: 巴里太太急切地问道：“怎么了？你哪里受伤了？”安妮倒抽了一口气，“是我的脚踝。”

paragraphs.en: She requested Diana to find her father and take her home, explaining that she couldn't walk or hop on one foot.
paragraphs.zh: 她请戴安娜去找她的父亲，带她回家，并解释说她无法走路或单脚跳跃。

paragraphs.en: Marilla was picking apples in the orchard when Mr. Barry arrived with Mrs. Barry and a group of girls trailing behind. He carried Anne, whose head rested limply against his shoulder. Marilla's heart raced as she realized how dear Anne had become to her.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉正在果园里捡苹果，这时巴里先生带着巴里太太和一群女孩 arrived 后面跟着走了进来。他怀里抱着安妮，安妮的头无力地靠在他的肩膀上。玛丽拉的心跳加速了，她意识到自己对安妮的感情已经变得如此深厚。

paragraphs.en: She admitted that she liked Anne very much and now knew Anne was more precious than anything else in the world.
paragraphs.zh: 她承认自己非常喜欢安妮，现在觉得安妮比世界上任何东西都珍贵。

paragraphs.en: Marilla hurried down the slope, her face pale and shaken, asking Mr. Barry, "What has happened to her?" Anne lifted her head to answer.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉匆匆下了山坡，脸色苍白而激动，她问巴里先生：“她出了什么事？”安妮抬起头来回答。

paragraphs.en: Marilla was relieved yet sharp when Anne fell off the ridgepole at the party. "Bring her in here," she said to Mr. Barry, who laid Anne on the sofa. "The child has fainted!"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉松了口气，但还是有些紧张，当安妮在晚会上从横梁上摔下来时。她对巴里先生说：“快把她带进来。”巴里先生把安妮放在沙发上后，玛丽拉说道：“这孩子晕过去了！”

paragraphs.en: Anne had indeed fainted due to pain from a broken ankle. Matthew quickly fetched the doctor, who confirmed the severity of the injury.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮确实因踝骨骨折而昏了过去。马修迅速请来了医生，医生确认了伤势的严重性。

paragraphs.en: That night, Marilla found Anne lying pale in the east gable. "Aren't you sorry for me, Marilla?" Anne asked plaintively.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉发现安妮苍白地躺在东屋的床上。“玛莉拉，你为我难过吗？”安妮哀求道。

paragraphs.en: "It was your own fault," replied Marilla, adjusting the blind and lighting a lamp.
paragraphs.zh: “这都是你自己造成的。”玛丽拉回答道，调整了窗帘，并点亮了一盏灯。

paragraphs.en: Anne continued, "And that's why you should be sorry too. The thought it’s all my doing makes it harder." She sighed.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮继续说：“这也是你应该感到遗憾的原因。想到这一切都是我的错，让我感觉更糟了。”她叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "If I could blame someone else, I'd feel better."
paragraphs.zh: “如果能怪罪到别人头上，我会好受些。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla responded, "I would have stayed on solid ground if dared to walk the ridgepole. Such nonsense!"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“要是敢走那根椽子，我宁愿站在地上。这纯粹是胡说八道！”

paragraphs.en: Anne admitted, "But you have such strength of mind. I don't. I couldn’t bear Josie Pye's scorn. She would have mocked me forever.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮承认，“但是你有坚强的意志力。我没有，我无法忍受乔西·派伊的轻蔑。她会永远嘲笑我。”

paragraphs.en: I think I’ve been punished enough; so please don’t be too cross with me."
paragraphs.zh: 我想我已经受够了惩罚，所以请不要对我太生气。

paragraphs.en: Marilla comforted, "There, there, I’m not cross. You’re unlucky but will suffer the consequences." She then urged Anne to eat some supper.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉安慰道：“别担心，别担心，我并没有生气。你只是倒霉了，自食其果。”说完，她催促安妮快吃点晚饭。

paragraphs.en: Anne often thanked her imagination during the long, dull seven weeks that followed. However, she relied on it less than on her visitors. Every day brought at least one schoolgirl to see her, bearing flowers, books, and tales from the Avonlea youth.
paragraphs.zh: 在随后漫长而单调的七个星期里，安妮经常感谢自己的想象力。不过她对想象的依赖远不如对来访者的依赖。每天至少会有一位女同学来看望她，带来鲜花、书籍和埃文利年轻人的故事。

paragraphs.en: Anne was overjoyed to return to her room, limping across the floor with Marilla's help. "Everyone has been so good," she sighed happily. "It’s not pleasant being laid up, but there are bright sides.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮非常高兴能回到自己的房间，在玛丽拉的帮助下一瘸一拐地走进去。“大家都对我这么好，”她幸福地叹了口气，“虽然躺在床上不太舒服，但也有一些值得安慰的地方。”

paragraphs.en: I found out how many friends I have. Even Superintendent Bell came to see me, and he is a fine man. He could get over his habit of saying prayers as if he didn't mean them with some effort.
paragraphs.zh: 我发现自己有很多朋友。就连贝尔督学也来看我了，他是个正直的人。尽管他改掉嘴里常常念叨祈祷词却似乎不以为意的习惯需要一些努力，但他还是做到了。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan visited me fourteen times—quite an achievement for a minister's wife! She’s such a cheerful person; she never blames or lectures. Josie Pye also came to see me, and I received her politely because I think she was sorry about the dare.
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太来访十四次——真是牧师夫人的一大成就！她是个开朗的人，从不责备或说教。乔西·派也来看我了，出于我认为她对那次挑战感到抱歉的原因，我还是礼貌地接待了她。

paragraphs.en: Diana has been my faithful friend, visiting every day to cheer me up. I can't wait to go back to school; the new teacher is described as sweet with lovely curly hair and fascinating eyes. She dresses beautifully, and the girls are preparing a dialogue for Friday.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜一直是我的忠实朋友，每天都来探望我，让我振作起来。我迫不及待地想要回到学校；新来的老师被形容为甜美可人，留着可爱的卷发，眼睛更是迷人。她的打扮十分出色，女孩子们正在准备周五的对话表演。

paragraphs.en: Miss Stacy also takes them on field days in the woods and has physical culture exercises."
paragraphs.zh: 斯蒂西小姐还带她们去树林里参加野营日活动，并进行体能训练。

paragraphs.en: Marilla listened patiently as Anne recounted her experiences. "Mrs. Lynde always told me I would be better," Anne continued, "but she didn't really believe it. Diana and Ruby Gillis are working on a dialogue called 'A Morning Visit.'
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉耐心地听着安妮讲述她的经历。“雷切尔·林德夫人总是告诉我，我会变得更好，”安妮继续说道，“但她并不真的相信这一点。戴安娜和鲁比·吉尔斯正在合作编写一个对话剧本，名叫《晨访》。”

paragraphs.en: Miss Stacy takes them to study ferns, flowers, and birds every Friday afternoon. And they have physical culture exercises in the mornings and evenings. Mrs. Lynde thinks all this is due to having a lady teacher, but I believe it must be splendid."
paragraphs.zh: 斯泰西小姐每周五下午带她们去研究蕨类植物、花朵和鸟类。早上和晚上则进行体能锻炼。雷切尔·林德太太认为这一切都是因为有了女老师，但我相信这一定非常精彩。

paragraphs.en: Anne's excitement was palpable as she imagined her return to school and the new teacher.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮兴奋之情溢于言表，她想象着重返校园和那位新老师的情景。

paragraphs.en: Marilla observed, "It’s clear, Anne, that falling from the Barry roof hasn’t affected your tongue in any way."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉观察着安妮，说道：“显然，安妮，从巴里家的屋顶摔下来并没有影响你的口舌。”

paragraphs.en: Anne's face flushed as she realized her slip.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的脸颊顿时涨得通红，她意识到自己失言了。
